title: fix(rest)!: format=json honours an explicit ?fields=
body:
Fixes #24183

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

**BREAKING** (a served-set narrowing at a REST door): with `?fields=`, each row of `GET /api/v1/data/:object/export?format=json` now carries exactly the named keys. It ships as `minor` under the launch-window convention. The changeset carries the same `Clause-②` line and one ADR-0087 disposition (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). This narrowing owes one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of record before the queue.

**Why `Fixes`:** this PR now lands both halves of the card. The explicit-`fields` half was the first round. The no-`fields` half was a fork: the claim's premise failed when measured (see "The no-`fields` fork" below), and the seat decided **D** in comment 6238218754. JSON without `fields` writes each row as the read returns it, which is what `QuerySchema.fields` declares (optional, "Fields to retrieve": absent means no projection). Patch round 1 pins that answer through the real route, `id` included, and the route doc states it. The fork section below is kept as the measurement record. *(This paragraph and the first line were edited by the seat; the dev writes the body once.)*

## What changed

- `packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts`, JSON arm of the export handler: when `?fields=` names columns, each row is cut to the resolved `fields` list (`pickExportKeys`), the same list the CSV and XLSX arms write. `formatRowForJson` then formats the row as before. Keys come out in list order. A named key the read did not return is left out of the row. It is not written as `null`.
- `fieldsExplicit` records that the caller named the columns. Nothing after it narrows or reorders an explicit list: the hidden-field filter, the FLS projection and the masked-row fallback all run only on the schema-derived default. So the JSON arm reads the one resolved column list and does not define a second one.
- The route's doc comment for `fields=` now says what each format does with it, and that JSON without `fields` writes each row as the read returns it.
- Not changed: the CSV and XLSX arms and their default column set, `formatRowForJson` and `export-format.ts`, `stripSearchCompanionFromRead`, `packages/objectql`, `packages/spec` and objectui. `format=json` without `fields` is byte-for-byte the same as before.

## Does the CSV arm always write some extra key? Measured: no

`?format=csv&fields=title` returns the single column `Title`, both on the showcase and in the unit pin. So the JSON projection mirrors nothing beyond the named keys.

## Reach, re-measured on `examples/app-showcase`

Setup: a `pnpm dev -- --fresh` boot of this worktree, signed in as the seeded admin. The shipped admin sets carry no `allowExport`, so I saved an environment permission set granting `allowRead` and `allowExport` on `showcase_task` and assigned it to the admin.

`GET /api/v1/data/showcase_task/export?format=json&fields=title`, 10 rows:

- before (`8a88901be`): 25 keys per row: `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `organization_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `owner_id`, `owning_business_unit_id`, `title`, `project`, `assignee`, `status`, `priority`, `estimate_hours`, `progress`, `done`, `due_date`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `location`, `cover`, `labels`, `notes`, `sync_status`, `sync_error`.
- after (this branch): every row is exactly `{ "title": … }`.

After the fix, `?format=json&fields=status,title,id,organization_id,__search` returns rows that carry `status`, `title`, `id` and `organization_id`, in that order. `__search` is absent because the read strips it. The list door answers the same way: in the unit harness, `GET /data/note?$select=title,__search` returns rows with `title` only.

Unchanged after the fix: the no-`fields` JSON key set, and the CSV header with and without `fields=title`. I compared shapes, because each fresh boot seeds new ids.

## The no-`fields` fork: the claim's premise, measured, fails

The claim's premise was that the default set (schema fields minus `hidden`, ∩ FLS-readable) contains `id` and every key the JSON re-import reads back. It does not contain `id`. `showcase_task` does not declare `id`, and the registry injects no `id` field, so `id` is not in the schema the default reads from.

- No-`fields` JSON today: the 25 keys listed above.
- The default set: 22 keys, matching the CSV no-`fields` header label for label. They are `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`, `owner_id`, `title`, `project`, `assignee`, `status`, `priority`, `estimate_hours`, `progress`, `done`, `due_date`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `created_at`, `location`, `cover`, `labels`, `notes`, `sync_status`, `sync_error`.
- The default would drop three keys:
  - `id`;
  - `organization_id`, which is hidden and carries `Default Organization`;
  - `owning_business_unit_id`, which is hidden and null.

The import runner reads `id` back: it keeps a supplied id on insert and matches on it for update and upsert. I re-imported the export through `POST /api/v1/data/showcase_task/import` with `format: json` and `dryRun: true`:

| rows sent | `writeMode` / `matchFields` | answer |
|---|---|---|
| no-`fields` JSON as served today | `upsert` / `id` | 10 updated, 0 created |
| the same rows cut to the default set | `upsert` / `id` | 0 updated, **10 created**: every record duplicated |
| the same rows cut to the default set | `update` / `id` | 10 skipped |

The options and a recommendation are in the `os-dev-report` comment on #24183, for the seat to decide.

## Tests

`packages/rest/src/export-json-fields.test.ts` exercises the real export route: a real `RestServer` on a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` on a real `ObjectQL`, with a better-sqlite3 `:memory:` driver. The companion is declared by its real producer. The protocol's `findData` is observed, so every pin shows the rows the read handed over next to what the route answered.

- CSV control (the measurement above): `?fields=title` writes the single `Title` column, while the read returned `id`, `title`, `internal_code` and `done`.
- JSON `?fields=title`: every row is exactly `{ title }`.
- JSON `?fields=done,internal_code,title,id`: keys come out in list order, and values keep the export formatting (`done` becomes `是` / `否`).
- JSON `?fields=title,__search`: the stripped companion is absent from the row and is never written as `null`. For the same list, CSV writes an empty `Search Index` column.
- JSON over two chunks (60 rows, `page=50`, two reads): every row carries exactly `id`.
- JSON with no security service composed: the projection still holds.

**Ablation**, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. The anchor must hit, and the restore is checked against the blob. The test reaches `data-action-routes.ts` through relative `./rest-server` imports, so it runs from `src/` and does not involve `dist/`.

- Mutation: `const row = fieldsExplicit ? pickExportKeys(rows[i], fields!) : rows[i];` became `const row = rows[i]; /* ablated-24183 */`. The anchor count went from 1 to 0, and the blob from `e78162e654a3` to `4c922008fbbb`.
- Result: **5 failed, 1 passed**. All five JSON pins went red. For example, `expected [ [ 'id', 'created_at', …(4) ], …(1) ] to deeply equal …` on the order pin. The CSV control stayed green, as it should, since the mutation leaves the CSV arm alone.
- Restore leg: the blob after restore is `e78162e654a3`, which equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

Suite runs on `881f6797e`:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test`: exit 0, 293 files passed, 6019 tests passed, 326 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck`: exit 0. The new test file is in the `tsconfig.test.json` program (`--listFiles`: 1 hit).
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` on the two changed source files: exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on `881f6797e`: 63 derived commands, all exit 0. The `--ran` reconciliation answers: 63 derived, 63 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, every exit code recorded.
- Not run locally: `test:repo` (CI's `Test Core`).

## Acceptance notes

- Without `?fields=`, the export's default columns for CSV and XLSX do not carry `id` on an object that does not declare it. That was already true before #24178: on the showcase, neither #24178's before-header (at `b0fe9fad4`) nor the header at `8a88901be` carries `ID`. So a CSV export cannot re-import onto its own records by `id`. This matches the route's documented default (schema fields), so it is noted here and not filed. It bears on the fork above.
- If a named key is one the read did not return, CSV and XLSX write an empty cell and JSON leaves the key out. JSON follows the list door's `$select` here, not the CSV cell.
